text.p: Typhoon Carlo, with 105 mph winds, is centered about 200 miles north of Agrihan in the northern Mariana Islands, moving north at 8 mph. Carlo will begin to weaken while moving northward over open water this period, threatening only shipping.

Hurricane Lili remains a threat to shipping. The center of the storm is 1460 miles west southwest of the Azores, moving east northeast at 5 mph. Top wind are 80 mph, and weakening is expected this period while the storm increases its foward speed to the east northeast while losing tropical characteristics.

Tropical Cyclone 05A has top winds near 65 mph and should strengthen to near 70 mph before landfal. The storm is moving to the north and is expected to make landfall in Gujarat in 12 hours with heavy rain and strong wind. Flooding may occur over Gujarat and far southern Pakistan.

A disturbance is still causing squalls in through the Andaman Islands of the southeast Bay of Bengal. It is somewhat of a risk to shipping in the area. The threat to shipping may increase if the storm develops further, which it may.
